title: Optimize config diff -> runtime knobs: safety notes + pre-gate validation ideas (working)
body:
Context / why this exists
- Optimize will propose config diffs that map to serving runtime knobs (batching, prefix/KV caching, quant profiles).
- Some combinations are “legal” but meaningfully change output (or cause rare correctness bugs / OOM / latency cliffs).
- Goal: catalog what’s risky, what’s safe-by-construction, and what we can cheaply validate BEFORE we spend GPU on eval gates.

Audience
- Runtime + Optimize engineers implementing config-diff schema + validators (Benji, Jordan).
- Applied ML wants to know which diffs require stricter gates.

Non-goals
- Not a full PRD. Not deciding thresholds. This is runtime-centric guardrails.

---
Config diff schema (runtime view)
Assumption: Optimize emits a typed diff with explicit “change_type” and “old/new” values, and a target scope.
Required fields (runtime needs these for safe validation):
- scope: route_id (or service/endpoint), model_id, model_family, model_revision, region, hw_sku
- change_type: BATCHING | CACHE | QUANT_PROFILE (MVP)
- baseline_ref: config version id + runtime build id (helps reproduce)
- intended_effect: cost_savings_estimate + latency_impact_estimate (not strictly needed for correctness but useful for prioritizing)

Important: for validation we need to know:
- model architecture class (llama-like, mixtral-like/MoE, etc.)
- context length cap configured for the route
- streaming enabled?
- tool/function calling enabled? (structured output modes tend to be more sensitive)

---
Mapping: Optimize knobs -> runtime knobs

1) Batching policy updates
Optimize diff fields we expect:
- max_batch_size_tokens (or total_tokens_per_batch)
- max_concurrent_sequences
- batch_wait_ms (a.k.a. queue_delay)
- prefill_batching_mode: {aggressive | balanced | disabled}
- decode_batching_mode: {continuous | step}

Runtime knobs (current runtime naming; may diverge by backend):
- scheduler.max_tokens_per_batch
- scheduler.max_seqs
- scheduler.queue_delay_ms
- scheduler.prefill_policy
- scheduler.decode_policy
- scheduler.max_prefill_concurrency (sometimes derived)

Safety note:
- Batching itself shouldn’t change semantics, BUT in practice it can change:
  - truncation behavior if we cap prefill tokens per batch incorrectly
  - timeout/cancellation behavior leading to partial outputs
  - starvation or head-of-line blocking which changes “completion length” if clients have max_time
- So: treat batching changes as “usually safe” but still can trigger “effective output change” under client time budgets.

2) Prefix/KV caching settings
Optimize diff fields we expect:
- prefix_cache.enabled (bool)
- prefix_cache.max_entries (or max_bytes)
- prefix_cache.ttl_seconds
- kv_cache.reuse.enabled (bool) [careful: some internal modes are not safe across tokenization boundaries]
- kv_cache.partitioning: {per_route | per_tenant | global}
- kv_cache.keying_mode: {prompt_hash | canonicalized_prompt_hash | token_ids_hash}

Runtime knobs:
- cache.prefix.enable
- cache.prefix.capacity_bytes / entries
- cache.prefix.ttl_s
- cache.kv_reuse.enable
- cache.kv.scope
- cache.kv.key_mode

Safety note:
- Cache settings can absolutely change outputs if keying/canonicalization is wrong or scope leaks across tenants.
- Even when correct, caching interacts with:
  - tool calling (function name/schema often embedded in system prompt)
  - dynamic timestamps / request ids in prompts (canonicalization should not strip semantics)

3) Quantization profile changes
Optimize diff fields we expect:
- quant.profile_id (e.g., q8_0, fp8_w8a8, int4_awq, etc.)
- quant.kernel_family (optional): {triton | cutlass | vendor}
- quant.calibration_set_id (optional)
- quant.fallback_profile_id (required for safety)

Runtime knobs:
- engine.quant.profile
- engine.quant.kernel
- engine.quant.calibration
- engine.quant.fallback

Safety note:
- Quant changes are the most likely to affect output quality (and sometimes correctness if kernels are buggy on specific SKUs).
- Baseline must be defined per (model_family, model_revision, hw_sku). “Same profile” is not equivalent across SKUs.

---
Pre-gate validation: what we should reject BEFORE running evals
Idea: static validator in Optimize (ENG-3930) calls runtime “capabilities” endpoint or uses baked-in rules.

Validation categories
A) Structural validation (cheap)
- Unknown fields / missing required fields.
- Scope mismatch: diff claims model_family X but route is pinned to Y.
- Attempt to modify immutable fields (e.g., context length cap) via Optimize diffs (out of scope).

B) Capability validation (cheap-ish)
- Ensure target hw_sku supports proposed quant profile.
- Ensure runtime build supports requested scheduler mode.
- Ensure cache partitioning mode is allowed for route tier (enterprise vs self-serve policy).

C) Safety constraint validation (the big one)
- Block known-unsafe combinations immediately (see “unsafe catalog”).
- Apply conservative bounds (min/max) on numeric knobs to avoid latency cliffs and OOM.

D) Risk scoring (optional)
- Return a “risk_class” to gating system to select smoke vs full gates.

---
Unsafe / high-risk combinations catalog (living list)
(If we can encode these as rules with reason codes, great. If not, at least document.)

1) Quant profile + long context (OOM / correctness risk)
- If route max_context_tokens >= 64k AND quant.profile_id in {int4_awq, int4_gptq} => require full gates + runtime dry-run memory check.
- Reason: KV cache memory dominates; some int4 paths degrade stability when combined with paged KV at high seq length.
- Observed symptoms: rare NaNs under fp8/int4 on H100 when prefill batch > X (still investigating).

2) Aggressive prefill batching + streaming + low client timeout (effective output change)
- If streaming_enabled=true AND scheduler.queue_delay_ms > 50ms => warn/require sign-off (or force smoke gate that uses strict client-side deadline).
- Reason: we can cause truncation at client layer; looks like quality regression but it’s behavior/regression.

3) KV reuse across tenants or routes (security + correctness)
- cache.kv.scope = global OR per_route when route is multi-tenant => hard block.
- Only allow per_tenant for hosted API, and for Dedicated allow per_cluster if single-tenant contract says OK.
- Reason: cross-tenant leakage risk (even if keys are hashed), plus “prompt collisions” can create wrong reuse.

4) Canonicalized prompt hashing when prompts contain dynamic segments
- If cache.key_mode = canonicalized_prompt_hash AND route has “dynamic_system_prompt=true” (feature flag) => block.
- Reason: canonicalization currently strips multiple whitespace and certain JSON key ordering; breaks semantics for structured output and tool calling prompts.
- Action: keep key_mode=token_ids_hash for those routes until canonicalizer v2.

5) Cache TTL too high + rolling prompt changes (staleness)
- If prefix_cache.enabled=true AND prefix_cache.ttl_seconds > 86400 (1 day) on routes with prompt_versioning=disabled => block.
- Reason: stale prefixes can survive prompt updates, leading to “why did output ignore new policy?” incidents.

6) Batching limits beyond tested envelope (OOM / tail latency)
- If scheduler.max_tokens_per_batch > runtime_defaults.max_tokens_per_batch_for(model_family, hw_sku) => block or require explicit override.
- We need a table per (model_family, hw_sku). For now, keep conservative caps.

7) Quant kernel family mismatch
- If quant.kernel_family specified and not in allowlist for hw_sku => block.
- Reason: wrong kernel selection may silently fall back to slower path, breaking cost/latency assumptions and confusing gating outcomes.

8) Mixed “prefill aggressive” with “decode step” on MoE (known performance cliff)
- model_family=MoE AND prefill_policy=aggressive AND decode_policy=step => warn + require smoke gate (performance-oriented) and full gate if applied to >X% traffic.
- Not a correctness issue, but leads to p99 blow-ups and then clients lower max_tokens etc., indirectly changing outputs.

---
Suggested rule format (for implementation)
We should standardize on:
- rule_id (stable)
- severity: BLOCK | WARN | INFO
- reason_code: short enum for audit logs
- message: human readable
- remediation: suggested change

Example:
- rule_id: RUNTIME_CACHE_SCOPE_001
- severity: BLOCK
- reason_code: KV_SCOPE_MULTI_TENANT
- message: "KV cache reuse scope 'global' not allowed for multi-tenant hosted routes. Use per_tenant."

---
Runtime “dry-run” checks worth adding (cheap runtime introspection)
If we can do a fast preflight without allocating full model weights:
- Memory estimate check:
  - Inputs: model_family, quant_profile, max_context_tokens, max_tokens_per_batch, max_seqs
  - Output: predicted peak VRAM (prefill+decode) + headroom threshold.
  - If > 90% VRAM => block (OOM risk) or auto-reduce batch cap.

- Kernel availability check:
  - Confirm quant kernels compiled/available for hw_sku + CUDA version.

- Cache compatibility check:
  - Validate key_mode supported for route features (tool calling, structured output).

Note: This preflight should run in < 1s and be callable by Optimize service. Ideally cached by (model_revision, hw_sku).

---
Repro / debugging hooks we should insist on
For every config diff that reaches eval gates, record:
- runtime build sha
- model_revision sha
- tokenizer version id
- exact resolved runtime config after applying diff (post-defaults)
- derived scheduler params (anything auto-tuned)

Otherwise we will not be able to reproduce “gate failed only in eu-west” type tickets.

---
Open questions / TODOs
- Do we treat “batch_wait_ms increase” as quality-risk or purely performance-risk? (I lean: quality-risk because it changes deadline interactions.)
- How do we encode “route has dynamic prompts” in a stable way for validation? (needs control-plane signal)
- Quant baseline selection: we need the canonical baseline per (model_family, model_revision, hw_sku). (ENG-3924/PR-19558 is doing this; we need runtime to agree on identity.)
- Need a policy decision on which rules are BLOCK vs WARN in MVP.

---
Near-term action items
- Noah: translate unsafe catalog into a first-pass validator spec for ENG-3930 (reason codes + messages).
- Sofia: provide safe bounds for scheduler.max_tokens_per_batch + max_seqs per hw_sku for top 5 model families.
- Omar: confirm which cache.key_mode values are safe with tool calling + structured output; propose allowlist.
- Grace/Arjun: provide quant profile allowlist per SKU + known-bad combos (esp long-context + paged KV).
- Benji/Jordan: ensure config-diff schema can carry hw_sku + route feature flags used by validators.

Appendix: quick glossary
- “prefix cache” = reuse computation for identical prefix prompts (prefill acceleration)
- “KV reuse” = reuse/retain key-value attention cache across requests (high risk unless strictly keyed)
- “smoke gates” = fast eval tier; “full gates” = broad prompt sets + stats
